drs.name: Defensive Runs Saved (DRS)
drs.description: Defensive Runs Saved (DRS) is a statistic that measures a player's overall defensive performance by quantifying the number of runs they save (or cost) compared to an average defender at their position.
drs.why: DRS is used to evaluate a player's ability to prevent runs through defense, including fielding, positioning, and throwing accuracy. A higher DRS indicates better defensive contributions.
drs.formula: DRS = (Outs Above Average) + (Plays Made vs. Expected) + (Position Adjustment)

sb.name: Stolen Bases (SB)
sb.description: Stolen bases occur when a base runner successfully advances to the next base while the pitcher is delivering the ball to the plate, without being tagged out.
sb.why: Stolen bases are used to assess a player's baserunning, speed and ability to advance on the basepaths without the ball being put in play. A higher number of stolen bases indicates more aggressiveness and effectiveness on the basepaths.
sb.formula: Stolen Bases = Number of times a player steals a base successfully

cs.name: Caught Stealing (CS)
cs.description: Caught stealing is a statistic that measures when a base runner attempts to steal a base but is thrown out by the catcher or another fielder.
cs.why: Caught stealing is used to assess a player's success rate and the effectiveness of the opposing team's defense, particularly the catcher’s ability to throw out runners and the pitcher’s ability to control the run-game.
cs.formula: Caught Stealing = Number of times a player is thrown out while attempting to steal a base

so.name: Strikeouts (K)
so.description: An out called when a batter accumulates three strikes.
so.why: Strikeouts are used to measure a batter's inability to make contact with the ball and can also reflect a pitcher's ability to generate swing-and-miss.
so.formula: Strikeouts = Number of strikeouts by the batter or pitcher

bb.name: Walks
bb.description: Walks are awarded to a batter when the pitcher throws four balls outside the strike zone, allowing the batter to reach first base without the need for a hit.
bb.why: Walks are used to evaluate a batter's patience, zone recognition and work the count in their favor. It also reflects the pitcher's control and ability to avoid giving free passes.
bb.formula: Walks = Number of times a batter receives a walk (four balls)

era.name: Earned Run Average (ERA)
era.description: ERA measures the average number of earned runs a pitcher allows per nine innings pitched.
era.why: ERA is used to assess a pitcher's effectiveness in preventing earned runs. A lower ERA generally indicates better pitching performance, but does not account for luck, park factors or defense.

ip.name: Innings Pitched (IP)
ip.description: Innings pitched measures the total number of innings a pitcher has completed during a game or season.
ip.why: Innings pitched is used to evaluate a pitcher's stamina and workload. More innings pitched indicates durability and effectiveness in staying in games.
ip.formula: Innings Pitched = Total number of innings a pitcher completes

w.name: Wins (W)
w.description: A win is credited to a pitcher when they are the pitcher of record when their team takes the lead and maintains it.
w.why: Wins are used to measure a pitcher's ability to contribute to a team’s victory, though it can sometimes be influenced by factors outside the pitcher's control.
w.formula: Wins = Number of games in which the pitcher is credited with the win

l.name: Losses (L)
l.description: A loss is charged to a pitcher when their team is losing at the time the pitcher is removed from the game.
l.why: Losses are used to measure a pitcher's effectiveness, though they can be impacted by the team's offensive support and other factors outside the pitcher’s control.
l.formula: Losses = Number of games in which the pitcher is charged with the loss

whip.name: Walks and Hits per Inning Pitched (WHIP)
whip.description: WHIP measures the number of base runners a pitcher allows per inning pitched, combining walks and hits.
whip.why: WHIP is used to assess a pitcher's ability to prevent runners from reaching base. A lower WHIP generally indicates a better pitcher.

baa.name: Batting Average Against (BAA)
baa.description: Batting Average Against measures how often batters get a hit off a pitcher.
baa.why: BAA is used to assess how effective a pitcher is in preventing opposing batters from getting hits.

qs.name: Quality Start (QS)
qs.description: A quality start occurs when a pitcher completes at least six innings and allows three or fewer earned runs.
qs.why: Quality starts are used to assess a pitcher’s ability to give their team a competitive chance by pitching deep into games and limiting earned runs.
qs.formula: Quality Start = If innings pitched ≥ 6 and earned runs ≤ 3

sv.name: Saves (SV)
sv.description: A save is awarded to a pitcher who finishes a game in which their team maintains a lead, while meeting specific criteria for the situation (e.g., pitching at least one inning).
sv.why: Saves are used to measure a relief pitcher’s effectiveness in closing out games and preserving a lead.
sv.formula: Save = (Pitcher finishes game with lead and pitches at least one inning; or enters game with a lead of no more than three runs and records at least one out)

bs.name: Blown Saves (BS)
bs.description: Blown saves occur when a pitcher fails to preserve a lead they are brought in to protect.
bs.why: Blown saves are used to measure a reliever's inability to successfully close a game, indicating missed opportunities to secure a win.
bs.formula: Blown Save = When a pitcher fails to hold a lead they were brought in to protect

er.name: Earned Runs (ER)
er.description: Earned runs are runs that score as a direct result of the pitcher's actions, excluding runs due to errors or passed balls.
er.why: Earned runs are used to measure a pitcher’s effectiveness in preventing scoring, as they reflect runs the pitcher is directly responsible for.
er.formula: Earned Runs = Total number of runs allowed minus unearned runs due to errors or passed balls

ha.name: Hits Allowed (H)
ha.description: Hits allowed counts the number of hits a pitcher allows to batters during the course of a game.
ha.why: Hits allowed is used to assess how well a pitcher prevents batters from reaching base. A lower number of hits allowed generally indicates better performance.
ha.formula: Hits Allowed = Number of hits a pitcher allows

hitter_wrc_plus.name: Weighted Runs Created Plus (wRC+)
hitter_wrc_plus.description: wRC+ quantifies a player's offensive contributions while adjusting for league and park factors, with 100 being league average.
hitter_wrc_plus.why: wRC+ is used to evaluate a player's overall offensive performance while accounting for external factors like park and league variations. A score over 100 indicates better-than-average performance.

hitter_woba.name: Weighted On-Base Average (wOBA)
hitter_woba.description: wOBA measures a player's overall offensive value by giving different weights to various types of events (single, double, walk, home run, etc.).
hitter_woba.why: wOBA is used to more accurately assess a player's offensive contributions compared to traditional stats like OBP. It values walks and extra-base hits more effectively.
hitter_woba.formula: wOBA = (0.69 × Singles + 0.72 × Doubles + 0.90 × Triples + 1.24 × Home Runs + 0.30 × Walks + 0.72 × Hit by Pitch) / (At Bats + Walks + Hit by Pitch + Sacrifice Flies)

hitter_xwoba.name: Expected Weighted On-Base Average (xwOBA)
hitter_xwoba.description: xwOBA estimates a player's expected offensive performance based on the quality of contact they make (exit velocity, launch angle, etc.), without the influence of luck.
hitter_xwoba.why: xwOBA is used to assess how well a player is hitting the ball, independent of results like BABIP, providing a predictive measure of their true offensive ability.
hitter_xwoba.formula: xwOBA = wOBA based on Statcast data, considering exit velocity and launch angle.

hitter_bb_percent.name: Walk Rate (BB%)
hitter_bb_percent.description: Walk Rate (BB%) calculates the percentage of plate appearances in which a batter walks.
hitter_bb_percent.why: Walk rate is used to measure a player's plate discipline and ability to avoid swinging at pitches outside the strike zone. A higher walk rate indicates a better ability to get on base.

hitter_k_percent.name: Strikeout Rate (K%)
hitter_k_percent.description: Strikeout Rate (K%) calculates the percentage of plate appearances in which a batter strikes out.
hitter_k_percent.why: Strikeout rate is used to evaluate a player's plate discipline and contact ability. A lower strikeout rate indicates better contact skills.

hitter_babip.name: Batting Average on Balls in Play (BABIP)
hitter_babip.description: BABIP measures a player's batting average on balls put in play, excluding home runs, strikeouts, and walks.
hitter_babip.why: BABIP is used to assess a player's luck and batting skill when the ball is in play. A significantly high or low BABIP can indicate whether a player's performance is sustainable.
hitter_babip.formula: BABIP = (Hits - Home Runs) / (At Bats - Strikeouts - Home Runs + Sacrifice Flies)

hitter_iso.name: Isolated Power (ISO)
hitter_iso.description: ISO measures a player's ability to hit for extra bases, reflecting their raw power by isolating slugging percentage from batting average.
hitter_iso.why: ISO is used to evaluate a player's power-hitting ability, with a higher ISO indicating more extra-base hits, such as doubles, triples, and home runs.

hitter_bb_k.name: Walk-to-Strikeout Ratio (BB/K)
hitter_bb_k.description: BB/K measures the ratio of walks to strikeouts for a batter, offering insight into a player's plate discipline and strike zone judgment.
hitter_bb_k.why: BB/K is used to evaluate a batter's ability to avoid strikeouts and demonstrate patience at the plate. A higher ratio indicates better discipline and decision-making.

hitter_tb.name: Total Bases (TB)
hitter_tb.description: Total Bases calculates the total number of bases a player accumulates via hits, including singles, doubles, triples, and home runs.
hitter_tb.why: Total bases is used to measure a player's overall power and offensive contribution. A higher total bases count indicates a player who generates more extra-base hits.
hitter_tb.formula: TB = Singles + (2 × Doubles) + (3 × Triples) + (4 × Home Runs)

hitter_owar.name: Offensive Wins Above Replacement (oWAR)
hitter_owar.description: oWAR quantifies a player's total offensive value, taking into account their batting, baserunning, and overall ability to contribute to the team's runs.
hitter_owar.why: oWAR is used to measure a player's overall offensive impact, adjusted for park and league factors. A higher oWAR indicates a more valuable offensive player.

hitter_xba.name: Expected Batting Average (xBA)
hitter_xba.description: xBA estimates a player's batting average based on the quality of contact they make, considering factors like exit velocity and launch angle, while removing the influence of luck.
hitter_xba.why: xBA is used to predict a player's future batting average, accounting for factors that affect ball placement and contact quality. It is a better measure of a player's true talent than traditional batting average.
hitter_xba.formula: xBA = Calculated based on exit velocity, launch angle, and the league’s expected outcomes on similar hits.

hitter_xslg.name: Expected Slugging Percentage (xSLG)
hitter_xslg.description: xSLG estimates a player's slugging percentage based on the quality of contact they make, factoring in exit velocity and launch angle, excluding the influence of randomness.
hitter_xslg.why: xSLG is used to predict a player's future slugging performance by assessing the quality of their hits, offering a more accurate forecast than actual slugging percentage.
hitter_xslg.formula: xSLG = Calculated based on exit velocity and launch angle, considering league averages for similar batted balls.

hitter_avg_exit_velocity.name: Average Exit Velocity
hitter_avg_exit_velocity.description: Average Exit Velocity measures the average speed of the ball as it leaves the bat, indicating how hard a player is hitting the ball on average.
hitter_avg_exit_velocity.why: Average exit velocity is used to evaluate a player's raw power and ability to hit the ball with authority. Higher exit velocities generally lead to more extra-base hits.
hitter_avg_exit_velocity.formula: Average Exit Velocity = (Sum of all exit velocities) / (Total number of batted balls)

hitter_barrel_percent.name: Barrel%
hitter_barrel_percent.description: Barrel% measures the percentage of a player's batted balls that result in barrels—batted balls hit with the optimal combination of exit velocity and launch angle.
hitter_barrel_percent.why: Barrel% is used to assess how often a player is making high-quality contact, as barrels are strongly correlated with offensive success. A higher barrel percentage indicates better power and contact ability.
hitter_barrel_percent.formula: Barrel% = (Number of barrels / Total batted balls) × 100

hitter_hardhit_percent.name: HardHit%
hitter_hardhit_percent.description: HardHit% calculates the percentage of a player's batted balls that have an exit velocity of 95 mph or higher, indicating hard contact.
hitter_hardhit_percent.why: HardHit% is used to assess a player's ability to consistently hit the ball hard. A higher hard-hit percentage generally correlates with better offensive output and more extra-base hits.

hitter_chase_percent.name: Chase%
hitter_chase_percent.description: Chase% measures the percentage of pitches outside the strike zone that a batter swings at.
hitter_chase_percent.why: Chase% is used to evaluate a player's plate discipline, with a lower percentage indicating better pitch selection and the ability to avoid swinging at bad pitches.
hitter_chase_percent.formula: Chase% = (Pitches swung at outside the strike zone / Total pitches outside the strike zone) × 100

hitter_whiff_percent.name: Whiff%
hitter_whiff_percent.description: Whiff% calculates the percentage of swings a batter takes that result in a miss (strikeout swing).
hitter_whiff_percent.why: Whiff% is used to assess a batter's ability to make contact with pitches. A lower whiff percentage indicates better contact skills and plate discipline.

sb_percent.name: Stolen Base Percentage (SB%)
sb_percent.description: Stolen Base Percentage measures a player's efficiency in stealing bases, calculated by the ratio of successful stolen bases to total steal attempts.
sb_percent.why: SB% is used to assess a player's success rate when attempting to steal bases. A higher SB% indicates a more efficient base runner.

sprint_speed.name: Sprint Speed
sprint_speed.description: Sprint Speed measures a player's maximum running speed over a certain distance, usually calculated based on a player's 90-foot sprint time.
sprint_speed.why: Sprint Speed is used to assess a player's raw speed, indicating how fast they can run from base to base, which directly impacts their ability to steal bases and cover ground defensively.
sprint_speed.formula: Sprint Speed = Maximum speed (feet per second) measured during a sprint over 90 feet

spd.name: Spd (Speed Score)
spd.description: Spd (Speed Score) is a composite measure of a player's overall speed, incorporating factors like stolen bases, runs, and the player's ability to take extra bases.
spd.why: Spd is used to evaluate a player's overall base-running ability, factoring in both stealing bases and taking extra bases on hits. A higher Spd indicates a faster player with good base-running instincts.
spd.formula: Spd = ((Stolen Bases × 2) + (Extra Bases Taken) - (Caught Stealing × 2)) / (Games Played)

bsr.name: BsR (Base Running Runs Above Average)
bsr.description: BsR is a metric that measures a player's overall base-running value, including stolen bases, extra bases taken, and avoided outs on the bases.
bsr.why: BsR is used to assess a player's base-running contributions to their team, accounting for all aspects of running the bases. A higher BsR indicates better base-running skills.
bsr.formula: BsR = Total Base Running Runs Above Average (calculated using a detailed model based on various base-running events)

wgdp.name: wGDP (Weighted Grounded Into Double Plays)
wgdp.description: wGDP quantifies the number of double plays a player grounds into, weighted to reflect the impact of these outs on the team's run-scoring potential.
wgdp.why: wGDP is used to measure a player's ability to avoid grounding into double plays, which can hurt offensive potential. A lower wGDP value is better, indicating fewer impactful double plays.
wgdp.formula: wGDP = (Grounded into Double Plays × Weighting factor based on the game's context)

oaa.name: Outs Above Average (OAA)
oaa.description: Outs Above Average calculates the number of outs a player records above the league average at their position, based on their fielding performance.
oaa.why: OAA is used to evaluate a player's defensive value by determining how many more outs they make compared to an average fielder at their position. A positive OAA indicates a strong defender.
oaa.formula: OAA = (Total Outs Made by Player - Expected Outs by League Average) + Park and Position Adjustments

uzr.name: Ultimate Zone Rating (UZR)
uzr.description: UZR is a defensive metric that evaluates a player's fielding by comparing the number of plays they make with the number of plays an average fielder at their position would make.
uzr.why: UZR is used to assess a player's defensive range and effectiveness at making plays, considering their positioning, zone coverage, and errors. A higher UZR indicates better defense.
uzr.formula: UZR = (Plays Made - Plays Expected) + Adjustments for Park and Position

fielding_percent.name: Fielding Percentage (Fielding%)
fielding_percent.description: Fielding Percentage measures a player's defensive efficiency, calculated as the ratio of successful fielding attempts (putouts and assists) to total chances (putouts, assists, and errors).
fielding_percent.why: Fielding percentage is used to assess a player's basic ability to make plays without committing errors. However, it does not account for range or the difficulty of plays.

arm_strength.name: Arm Strength
arm_strength.description: Arm Strength measures the power of a player's throwing arm, particularly for infielders and outfielders, reflecting the ability to make strong, accurate throws over long distances.
arm_strength.why: Arm strength is used to evaluate a player's ability to throw accurately and with velocity, which is crucial for preventing extra bases and turning double plays.
arm_strength.formula: Arm Strength = Measured by velocity of throws, average arm strength score (e.g., mph of throws from outfield or infield)

outfield_assists.name: Outfield Assists
outfield_assists.description: Outfield Assists tracks the number of times an outfielder successfully throws out a runner attempting to advance to another base.
outfield_assists.why: Outfield assists are used to measure a player's defensive value in the outfield, particularly their ability to stop runners from advancing. More outfield assists indicate stronger defensive skills.
outfield_assists.formula: Outfield Assists = Total number of successful throws resulting in a runner being thrown out

errors.name: Errors
errors.description: Errors track the number of fielding mistakes made by a player, such as misplays, dropped balls, or throws that result in a base runner being safe when they should have been out.
errors.why: Errors are used to evaluate a player's defensive reliability. Fewer errors indicate better defense, although errors alone don’t provide a full picture of a player's overall defense.
errors.formula: Errors = Total number of mistakes or misplays by a player

dwar.name: Defensive WAR (dWAR)
dwar.description: Defensive WAR measures a player's total defensive contribution to their team, calculating the number of wins they add through their defense, adjusted for position and league average.
dwar.why: dWAR is used to assess the overall impact of a player's defense, providing a single number that reflects how much value they add to their team’s defensive performance.
dwar.formula: dWAR = (Defensive Runs Above Average / Runs per Win) + Park and Position Adjustments

catcher_cera.name: Catcher's ERA (CERA)
catcher_cera.description: Catcher's ERA calculates the earned run average (ERA) for pitchers when a specific catcher is behind the plate. It measures the pitcher's performance with that catcher, providing insight into how the catcher handles the pitching staff.
catcher_cera.why: CERA is used to evaluate a catcher's ability to manage pitchers and prevent runs from scoring. A lower CERA suggests a catcher is effective in guiding pitchers to success.
catcher_cera.formula: CERA = (Earned Runs Allowed by Pitchers / Innings Pitched by Pitchers) × 9

catcher_fraa.name: Framing Runs Above Average (FRAA)
catcher_fraa.description: Framing Runs Above Average measures how many runs a catcher saves or costs by receiving pitches in a way that influences the umpire's calls, especially on borderline pitches.
catcher_fraa.why: FRAA is used to evaluate a catcher's ability to 'frame' pitches and turn borderline pitches into strikes, which can have a significant impact on a pitcher’s performance. A positive FRAA suggests a catcher is good at framing.
catcher_fraa.formula: FRAA = (Strike calls on borderline pitches) - (Ball calls on borderline pitches)

catcher_cs_percent.name: Caught Stealing Percentage (CS%)
catcher_cs_percent.description: Caught Stealing Percentage measures the percentage of runners caught attempting to steal a base compared to the total stolen base attempts.
catcher_cs_percent.why: CS% is used to assess a catcher's ability to throw out base stealers. A higher CS% indicates a catcher with strong arm strength and good timing on throws.

catcher_pop_time.name: Pop Time
catcher_pop_time.description: Pop Time measures the time it takes for a catcher to go from receiving a pitch to throwing it to second base on an attempted steal. It reflects the catcher's arm strength and release speed.
catcher_pop_time.why: Pop Time is used to evaluate a catcher's quickness and arm strength, which are crucial for throwing out runners attempting to steal bases.
catcher_pop_time.formula: Pop Time = Time (in seconds) from pitch reception to the throw reaching second base

catcher_block.name: Blocking Runs Above Average (BLOCK)
catcher_block.description: Blocking Runs Above Average measures a catcher's ability to block pitches in the dirt and prevent runners from advancing. It quantifies the value a catcher adds by keeping balls in front of them.
catcher_block.why: BLOCK is used to assess a catcher's skill in preventing wild pitches or passed balls that lead to runners advancing, which can affect the game’s outcome.
catcher_block.formula: BLOCK = (Runs Saved by Blocking Pitches) - (Runs Allowed by Passed Balls and Wild Pitches)

catcher_rto.name: Runners Thrown Out (RTO)
catcher_rto.description: Runners Thrown Out tracks the total number of runners a catcher throws out attempting to steal a base, not factoring in those who reach safely.
catcher_rto.why: RTO is used to evaluate a catcher’s ability to control the running game by throwing out base stealers. It highlights a catcher's arm strength and timing.
catcher_rto.formula: RTO = Total number of runners caught stealing

catcher_sbrs.name: Stolen Base Runs Saved (SBRS)
catcher_sbrs.description: Stolen Base Runs Saved quantifies the number of runs a catcher saves by preventing stolen bases relative to the league average.
catcher_sbrs.why: SBRS is used to assess how effective a catcher is at preventing stolen bases, factoring in both the number of stolen bases prevented and the pitcher's performance while they are behind the plate.
catcher_sbrs.formula: SBRS = (Stolen Bases Prevented - League Average Stolen Bases) × (Runs per Stolen Base)

catcher_draa.name: Defensive Runs Above Average (dRAA) for Catchers
catcher_draa.description: Defensive Runs Above Average for catchers (dRAA) is a comprehensive metric that evaluates a catcher's overall defensive value, including pitch framing, throwing, blocking, and handling pitchers.
catcher_draa.why: dRAA is used to evaluate a catcher's total defensive contributions. A higher dRAA indicates a more valuable defensive catcher.
catcher_draa.formula: dRAA = (Total Defensive Runs Saved by Catcher) - (League Average Defensive Runs)

pitcher_siera.name: SIERA
pitcher_siera.description: SIERA (Skill Interactive ERA) is an advanced pitching statistic that attempts to predict a pitcher's future ERA based on their skillset, including strikeouts, walks, and balls in play.
pitcher_siera.why: SIERA is used to assess a pitcher's overall effectiveness, adjusting for factors like park and defense. A lower SIERA indicates better pitching performance.

pitcher_xera.name: xERA
pitcher_xera.description: xERA (Expected ERA) is an advanced metric that estimates a pitcher's ERA based on factors like strikeouts, walks, and batted ball profile while adjusting for luck and defense.
pitcher_xera.why: xERA is used to evaluate a pitcher's true skill by filtering out luck and defensive variability. It gives a better understanding of how a pitcher should perform based on their skills.
pitcher_xera.formula: xERA = (Factors such as K%, BB%, GB%, Hard Contact Rate, and BABIP adjusted for defense)

pitcher_fip.name: FIP
pitcher_fip.description: FIP (Fielding Independent Pitching) measures a pitcher's effectiveness based solely on events within their control: strikeouts, walks, and home runs, removing the influence of defense and fielding.
pitcher_fip.why: FIP is used to evaluate a pitcher's true skill without the influence of fielders. A lower FIP indicates better pitching performance, as it focuses on controllable outcomes.
pitcher_fip.formula: FIP = ((13 × HR) + (3 × BB) - (2 × K)) / IP + Constant

pitcher_xfip.name: xFIP
pitcher_xfip.description: xFIP (Expected Fielding Independent Pitching) is a variation of FIP that adjusts for the league's home run rate. It uses a normalized home run per fly ball rate to account for luck in home runs allowed.
pitcher_xfip.why: xFIP is used to provide a more stable estimate of a pitcher's performance by removing the randomness of home runs allowed. It predicts future performance more reliably than FIP.
pitcher_xfip.formula: xFIP = ((13 × HR+ - HR) + (3 × BB) - (2 × K)) / IP + Constant

pitcher_babip.name: BABIP
pitcher_babip.description: BABIP (Batting Average on Balls in Play) measures how often a batter gets a hit on balls that are hit into the field of play, excluding home runs.
pitcher_babip.why: BABIP is used to evaluate the randomness of a pitcher's results on balls in play. A low BABIP may indicate luck or good defense, while a high BABIP may suggest a lack of control or poor defensive support.

pitcher_pitch_shapes.name: Pitch Shapes
pitcher_pitch_shapes.description: Pitch Shapes refer to the movement patterns of a pitch, including its break, speed, and trajectory. They help to analyze how pitches move and deceive batters.
pitcher_pitch_shapes.why: Pitch Shapes are used to assess a pitcher's ability to create movement with their pitches, influencing a batter's ability to make contact. Varied pitch shapes can make a pitcher more effective.
pitcher_pitch_shapes.formula: Pitch Shapes = Movement metrics for various pitches (e.g., horizontal break, vertical drop, speed)

pitcher_war.name: WAR (Wins Above Replacement)
pitcher_war.description: WAR is a comprehensive statistic that attempts to measure a player's overall contribution to their team, including batting, fielding, and pitching. For pitchers, it combines ERA, FIP, and other factors.
pitcher_war.why: WAR is used to quantify a pitcher's total value in one statistic. It compares the player's performance to a replacement-level player to determine how many wins they contribute to their team.
pitcher_war.formula: WAR = (Player's runs saved or created + Runs prevented) / (League's runs per win)

pitcher_lob_percent.name: LOB%
pitcher_lob_percent.description: LOB% (Left On Base Percentage) is the percentage of base runners a pitcher strands, i.e., the percentage of runners who do not score after reaching base.
pitcher_lob_percent.why: LOB% is used to evaluate a pitcher's ability to get out of jams and strand base runners. A high LOB% indicates effectiveness in high-leverage situations.
pitcher_lob_percent.formula: LOB% = (Innings Pitched - Earned Runs Allowed) / (Base Runners Allowed) × 100

pitcher_vfa.name: vFA (Velocity of Fastball)
pitcher_vfa.description: vFA measures the average velocity of a pitcher's fastball.
pitcher_vfa.why: vFA is used to assess a pitcher's fastball velocity, which can indicate the power of their arm and the potential for missing bats. A higher velocity generally makes it harder for batters to make solid contact.
pitcher_vfa.formula: vFA = Average velocity (mph) of the fastball pitches thrown

pitcher_k_percent.name: K%
pitcher_k_percent.description: K% (Strikeout Percentage) measures the percentage of batters a pitcher strikes out, calculated as the number of strikeouts divided by the number of batters faced.
pitcher_k_percent.why: K% is used to evaluate a pitcher's strikeout ability. A higher K% indicates a pitcher who is able to overpower batters and induce swings and misses.

pitcher_bb_percent.name: BB%
pitcher_bb_percent.description: BB% (Walk Percentage) measures the percentage of batters a pitcher walks, calculated as the number of walks divided by the number of batters faced.
pitcher_bb_percent.why: BB% is used to assess a pitcher's control and command. A lower BB% indicates a pitcher who is able to avoid issuing free passes.

pitcher_kbb_percent.name: K-BB%
pitcher_kbb_percent.description: K-BB% is the difference between a pitcher's strikeout percentage (K%) and walk percentage (BB%), providing insight into their control and dominance on the mound.
pitcher_kbb_percent.why: K-BB% is used to evaluate a pitcher's overall effectiveness by looking at their ability to miss bats and avoid walks. A higher K-BB% indicates better command and dominance.

pitcher_gb_percent.name: GB%
pitcher_gb_percent.description: GB% (Ground Ball Percentage) measures the percentage of balls in play that are hit on the ground, as opposed to fly balls or line drives.
pitcher_gb_percent.why: GB% is used to evaluate a pitcher's ability to induce ground balls, which typically result in fewer extra-base hits and are often easier to turn into outs. A higher GB% is generally favorable for pitchers.

pitcher_era_plus.name: ERA+
pitcher_era_plus.description: ERA+ (Adjusted ERA) is a metric that adjusts a pitcher's ERA for the league average, park factors, and other external influences, with 100 being average and each point above or below representing a percentage better or worse than average.
pitcher_era_plus.why: ERA+ is used to provide a league- and park-adjusted version of ERA, allowing for comparisons of pitchers across different contexts. A higher ERA+ indicates better-than-average pitching.
pitcher_era_plus.formula: ERA+ = ((League ERA / Player's ERA) × 100) × Park Adjustment

wpa.name: WPA (Win Probability Added)
wpa.description: WPA is a statistic that measures the change in a team's probability of winning a game as a result of a player's performance. It quantifies the impact of a player's actions on the outcome of a game by comparing the team's win probability before and after the event.
wpa.why: WPA is used to assess a player's contributions to a team's likelihood of winning in specific moments. It is especially useful for evaluating a player's performance in high-leverage situations (e.g., late innings or close games).
wpa.formula: WPA = (Win Probability After Event) - (Win Probability Before Event)

clutch_wpa.name: Clutch WPA
clutch_wpa.description: Clutch WPA measures the change in win probability from a player's performance in high-leverage situations, where the game's outcome is more uncertain and has a higher impact on the final result.
clutch_wpa.why: Clutch WPA is used to evaluate how a player performs in crucial situations, often with the game on the line. A positive Clutch WPA indicates a player who thrives under pressure.
clutch_wpa.formula: Clutch WPA = WPA in High-Leverage Situations

wpa_per_li.name: WPA/LI (Win Probability Added per Leverage Index)
wpa_per_li.description: WPA/LI normalizes WPA by the leverage of the situation. It provides a way to evaluate a player's impact on the game, adjusting for whether the situation was high or low-leverage. A higher WPA/LI suggests that a player had a significant impact in high-leverage moments.
wpa_per_li.why: WPA/LI is used to assess a player's performance relative to the leverage of the situation, helping to distinguish players who impact games in critical moments from those who perform well in low-leverage situations.

gw_rbi.name: Game-Winning RBI (GW-RBI)
gw_rbi.description: Game-Winning RBI is a statistic that tracks the RBI that results in the go-ahead run for the winning team in a game. It is a way to evaluate a player's ability to drive in runs in crucial moments.
gw_rbi.why: GW-RBI is used to highlight a player's ability to produce runs when it matters most, particularly in moments where they contribute to the winning run.
gw_rbi.formula: GW-RBI = RBI that results in the go-ahead run in a win

stuff_plus.name: Stuff+
stuff_plus.description: Stuff+ is a statistic that measures the quality of a pitcher's raw pitching abilities, including pitch velocity, movement, and overall effectiveness. It adjusts for factors like park and league differences to provide a standardized evaluation of stuff across all pitchers.
stuff_plus.why: Stuff+ is used to evaluate a pitcher's pure stuff, focusing on the velocity and movement of their pitches. It is useful for comparing pitchers' raw skills while accounting for external factors like ballpark and league adjustments. A Stuff+ above 100 indicates above-average stuff.

location_plus.name: Location+
location_plus.description: Location+ is a metric that quantifies a pitcher's command by evaluating how accurately they can locate their pitches in the strike zone. It adjusts for factors such as pitch type and batter handedness to provide a more nuanced evaluation of command and placement.
location_plus.why: Location+ is used to assess how well a pitcher can execute their pitches, specifically how well they hit their spots within the strike zone. A higher Location+ score indicates superior pitch command, meaning the pitcher places their pitches more effectively. A Location+ above 100 is considered better than league average.
location_plus.formula: Location+ = (Pitch Placement Relative to the Strike Zone) / (League Average Command) × 100

pitching_plus.name: Pitching+
pitching_plus.description: Pitching+ is a comprehensive statistic that combines a pitcher’s Stuff+ and Location+ to provide a more holistic view of their overall pitching ability. It factors in both the quality of their pitches (Stuff) and their ability to place them effectively (Location).
pitching_plus.why: Pitching+ is used to evaluate a pitcher's overall skill set by combining their raw pitch quality and their command. A higher Pitching+ score indicates a pitcher who excels in both stuff and location, making them more effective overall.
